Almost certainly a later 20th-century clock sold under the Thwaites & Reed name, not a Victorian one.

lots.confidence_reason: Dial signature read clearly, but there is no price evidence of any kind, the movement maker is unread and it is unknown whether it runs, strikes or alarms.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 (enlarged): dial reads THWAITES & REED and LONDON, Roman numerals, alarm subdial numbered 1-12. Correction to the researcher: the large coil seen through the back glass (photos 4 and 5, enlarged) is a coiled wire GONG, not a going barrel, so this is a striking clock, not a timepiece. Two square winding arbors are on the backplate (going and strike trains), plus a lever at top left, probably a strike/silent selector. The glass panel on top is the escapement viewing window, not a plaque. There is a faint stamp at the base of the backplate that I could not read at 450x600. No photo of the base, the repeat button (if any) or a serial number. Case bright with light tarnish; glass intact; back door opens.
lots.condition: Looks clean and complete with key; glass intact; light tarnish. Running, strike, repeat and alarm function all unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Does it run, strike on the gong, repeat and alarm? Is there a maker's stamp or serial number on the backplate or base (for example a French or Swiss movement maker), and is it the original key? Any cracks to the dial or glass?
